newsitem.title: ISRAEL: HBO leases channel on Israel's Amos satellite.
newsitem.headline: HBO leases channel on Israel's Amos satellite.

text.p: U.S. pay-television company HBO has signed a five-year agreement to lease half a transponder on Israel's Amos-1 satellite, Spacecom Ltd said on Monday.

HBO will use Amos to distribute six pay-TV channels to cable television operators in Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic starting in March 1997 and will eventually add other countries. HBO has an option to lease the transponder for an additional five years.

"In Spacecom's view, this contract proves the technical and marketing success, in view of the fact that HBO is a leader in the use of satellites and leader in the pay TV market," the company said in a statement.
Koby Keret, Spacecom's marketing director, would not say what HBO was paying for the use of the transponder.

Amos-1 was launched last May by state-owned Israel Aircraft Industries (IAI), which operates the satellite. Spacecom, a private company that sells space and ground satellite services, has since leased Amos transponders to several European broadcasters, among them Poland's ATV, Romania's TV 91 and Germany's Spaceway.
The company said it was in advanced negotiations with other potential users.
